cards.explanation: The answer is mercy. It's the very first thing out of David's mouth: "Be merciful to me, O God…" (Psalm 56:1). He doesn't open with a speech or a plan. He just asks, plain and honest, like a man who knows exactly who to call. That's a good instinct to have, friends.

The answer is False. David says, "…for many proudly assail me." (Psalm 56:2). Many of them, and they pursue him all day long. That's not a couple of guys, friends, that's a whole parking lot of trouble.

The answer is that David puts his trust in God. He says, "When I am afraid, I put my trust in You." (Psalm 56:3). Notice he doesn't pretend the fear isn't there, friends. The fear shows up, and the trust shows up right behind it.

The answer is that the people after him are no match for God. David trusts God, says he will not be afraid, and then asks, "What can man do to me?" (Psalm 56:4). He's weighing the people against the God he trusts, and the people come up short. It's a question that already knows its answer.
The answer is twist. David says, "All day long they twist my words…" (Psalm 56:5). He says something, and they bend it into something else. I think that gets old fast.

The answer is True, and it's a heavy one. David says they "…watch my steps while they wait to take my life." (Psalm 56:6). This part of the psalm is serious, and David treats it that way. That's also why his trust in God matters so much here.
The answer is cast down. David prays, "In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations." (Psalm 56:7). Notice who he's asking, friends: he says it to God. Cast down is the request.
The answer is False. David says, "You have taken account of my wanderings." (Psalm 56:8). God has them counted. That's a comfort, especially for anybody who has felt like nobody's keeping track.
The answer is tears. David says, "Put my tears in Your bottle…" (Psalm 56:8). He's asking God to hold on to them. I think that's one of the tenderest lines in the whole psalm.

The answer is that his enemies will retreat. David says, "Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help." (Psalm 56:9). The day he calls out is the day they back off, friends. That's some powerful backup.
The answer is True. David says, "By this I will know that God is on my side." (Psalm 56:9). The retreat of his enemies is how he'll know. He's looking for that sign.

The answer is thank offerings. David says, "Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You." (Psalm 56:12). He mentions the vows and the thank offerings side by side. That's a grateful man right there.

The answer is death, and David says it plainly: "For You have delivered my soul from death…" (Psalm 56:13). Remember the enemies waiting to take his life (Psalm 56:6). Now he's giving thanks for being delivered.

The answer is to walk before God in the light of life. David says God delivered him "…that I may walk before God in the light of life." (Psalm 56:13). He's out of the dark and walking in the light. After a psalm full of fear, friends, that's a good place to land.
